subject: Discovery recap — Finly: P95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Finly: P95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and next steps. I’ve attached a one-page QoS requirements doc and a mutual action plan (MAP) we can iterate on.

Key pain points you shared:
- Customer-facing chat UI currently suffers from noticeable lag at peak times (especially during long request/response pairs).
- Streaming UX is inconsistent: some messages stream, others appear in a bulk update which harms perceived latency.
- Backend batch inference spikes cause increased p95 tail latency and client timeouts during end-of-month processing windows.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Frontend: React + web sockets for chat streaming.
- Inference: self-hosted model on GCP (n1 GPU instances), custom batching service, Redis for session state.
- Observability: Grafana + internal dashboards; sampling on traces but tail metrics are noisy.

Success criteria (you indicated these are must-haves):
- p95 generation latency <= 600ms for standard conversational requests (non-long form).
- For streaming UX: first byte streaming start <= 200ms; subsequent token throughput consistent to avoid janky UI.
- Support 500 concurrent active chat sessions during peak with <5% request queueing above target latency.
- No regressions in output quality after any quantization/optimization changes.

What we propose (next steps):
1) Redwood quick benchmark: we’ll run a lightweight 48-hour proof-of-concept (PoC) using a representative request set you provide to measure p95 and streaming behavior (we’ll need sample requests and a short traffic shape).
2) Engineering sync: schedule a 30–45 min call with our inference engineer (Aditya) to go over current batching, KV cache usage, and telemetry hooks we’ll need.
3) MAP: we’ll share an editable mutual action plan (attached). If Finly agrees, we’ll target an initial PoC start the week of April 5.

Open questions for you (helps us scope the PoC):
- Can you share a representative trace or sample requests (anonymized) and current p95 reports for the last 30 days?
- What percent of requests are short conversational vs long-form (>1024 tokens)?
- Any regulatory constraints on logs/telemetry leaving your VPC?

Next meeting suggestion: Tue Apr 6, 10:00am PT — 30 min with Aditya + Camila to align on telemetry and PoC plan.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites and the MAP link.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0187

Attachments: Finly_QoS_requirements.pdf, Finly_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finly.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly: P95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Thanks Camila — this is perfect and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) p95 target — 600ms is correct for our chat baseline. For long-form (document summarization) we can tolerate up to ~2s p95.
2) Concurrency — 500 concurrent *active* sessions is our immediate target; planning for 1500 in 6 months if growth continues.
3) Streaming UX — our front-end team has instrumented first-byte time but it’s noisy; we’ll send a small dataset of 200 representative traces and the last 30 days of p95 graphs (anonymized).
4) Telemetry — logs containing user IDs cannot leave our VPC; we can provide sanitized traces and a sample traffic replay via a signed S3 bucket.

We’re onboard for the PoC. The suggested Apr 6 slot works for Aditya’s sync.

Quick ask: can your benchmark simulate our current batching behavior (we batch up to 32 requests every 25ms right now) so we can see comparable tails?

—San
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Engineering, Finly
sanjay@finly.com | +1 415-555-0210
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly: P95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Sanjay — that helps a lot. A few notes: 

- Yes, we can configure the PoC to replay your batching behavior (batch size 32, 25ms batching window) to produce apples-to-apples tail metrics. We’ll also try a few variants (smaller windows, dynamic batching) to compare cost/latency tradeoffs.
- For telemetry, we’ll accept sanitized traces or a signed S3 replay. If anything needs to be local-only, we’ll provide an on-prem agent option for measurement.
- I’ve created a short MAP in the shared Drive (link below) and tentatively booked Apr 6, 10:00am PT with Aditya and our inference lead. Please accept the invite and upload traces to the S3 bucket or Drive folder.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/finly-discovery-notes
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/Finly

Next internal step: Aditya, looping you in — can you confirm which telemetry fields you need (logs/traces/sample payloads) and whether you prefer S3 replay or a sandbox endpoint?

Camila
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly: P95 latency targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Hi team — quick engineering checklist so the PoC is effective: 

Required from Finly before PoC start:
- Representative request set (200 sample requests + 20 long-form samples) — anonymized.
- Last 30 days p95 histogram and concurrency curve (CSV or Grafana snapshot).
- Current batching settings (you mentioned batch=32, 25ms) and whether batching is client-driven or buffered in the service.
- A test S3 bucket with read-only sample payloads OR temporary sandbox endpoint we can hit from our benchmark runner.

What we’ll measure in PoC:
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency for both short and long requests.
- First-byte streaming latency and token inter-arrival stability (measure variance over time).
- Queueing/backlog behavior under ramp to 500 and 1500 concurrent sessions.
- Output quality spot-checks for any quantization or optimization we apply.

If you can drop the artifacts to the S3 link or Drive by Mon Mar 30, we’ll prepare the benchmark and share a PoC runbook.

Thanks — I’ll prepare a short list of telemetry fields (trace_id, request_latency_ms, batch_size, token_start_time, token_inter_arrival_ms, model_variant) and share it right after this.

—Aditya
